canvas.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "canvas and playground container" — narrower than the prior "page/app background" meaning, now specifically the live-preview/demo container surface. Value moved off neutral.white (was briefly byte-identical to bg.surface/bg.subtle) to gray.100, one step past bg.subtle (gray.50), so it reads as a visually distinct container again. Contrast re-verified: text.primary 12.41:1, text.secondary 6.05:1 — both clear AA. Byte-identical to border.subtle (also gray.100) — nothing currently pairs the two, flagged here in case a future component draws a border.subtle border directly on bg.canvas.

surface.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "page, card, sheet and drawer background" — broadens from "card/panel surface" to cover every default content surface, not just cards. Value unchanged (white).

surface-raised.$description: Usage description added (2026-08-08): "an elevated surface (paired with a shadow)". Value unchanged (white, byte-identical to bg.surface in light mode — elevation here comes from the paired shadow, not a background difference).

subtle.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "hover fill for tertiary/ghost controls, dashboard panel, neutral accent" — broadens from hover-fill/zebra-striping to also cover dashboard panels and general neutral accents. Value unchanged (gray.50). History: swapped with canvas 2026-07-27, when subtle was defined as the barely-visible tint layered on top of white bg.surface.

subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-17), found adding Tag's whole-tag clickable/selectable mode — bg.subtle's own hover step, one primitive scale step further in the same direction bg.brand-subtle-hover/etc. already use (darken in light mode, lighten in dark mode). text.secondary (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral's own paired text) on gray.100 = 6.05:1, comfortably passes AA.

brand-subtle.$description: Moved from emerald.100 to emerald.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction (matching bg.info-subtle's earlier move). Dark theme moved correspondingly (emerald.900 → emerald.950). Real consumers re-verified: Avatar's text.link (emerald.700) on emerald.50 = 5.83:1 (was 5.37:1 on emerald.100); ListItem's selected state (text.primary, gray.900) on emerald.50 = 13.53:1 — both still comfortably pass AA.

brand-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses brand-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (emerald.100), same pattern as purple-light.json's bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.link (emerald.700) on emerald.100 = 5.37:1, comfortably passes AA.

brand-indicator.$description: New token (2026-08-16), found adding a `brand` tone to Badge — for non-text graphical status indicators. Reuses bg.brand's own light value directly (emerald.700 vs bg.surface = 6.08:1) since that already clears the 3:1 non-text floor comfortably. Dark theme needs a different value (emerald.400, 4.63:1) — see that theme's own description for why bg.brand's own dark value (emerald.500) only manages 3.41:1, thinner than desired for a dedicated indicator. Brand-specific (unlike the shared danger/warning/success/info-indicator tokens), since brand color itself varies per theme.

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — bg.danger, text.danger, border.danger, and icon.danger now deliberately share the same primitive step per mode (red.600 light / red.300 dark), replacing what were several narrow single-purpose tokens with one reused value per category, while staying independently-tracked tokens for future divergence. Light value unchanged (red.600, 5.10:1 vs bg.surface). This also retires bg.danger-indicator: that token existed only because bg.danger's old dark value (red.500) failed WCAG 1.4.11 outright for small standalone graphics (2.90:1 against dark bg.surface) — the new dark value (red.300, see emerald-dark.json) clears it comfortably, so every former bg.danger-indicator consumer now uses this token directly. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

danger-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — light value unchanged (red.700). Dark value moved from red.400 to red.200, one step lighter, following bg.danger's own dark move to red.300 (keeping the same relative hover-lightening gap). text.on-danger (red.900 as of this change) on red.200 (dark) = 10.68:1.

danger-subtle.$description: Moved from red.100 to red.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (red.900 → red.950). text.danger (red.700 at the time) on red.50 = 7.05:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.43:1 on red.100). Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated light tint, independent of text.danger's own value.

danger-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses danger-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (red.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.danger (red.700 at the time) on red.100 = 6.43:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching danger-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — bg.warning, text.warning, border.warning, and icon.warning now deliberately share the same primitive step per mode (amber.600 light / amber.300 dark), replacing what were several narrow single-purpose tokens with one reused value per category, while staying independently-tracked tokens for future divergence. Light value unchanged (amber.600, 4.78:1 vs bg.surface). This also retires bg.warning-indicator: unlike danger's own old dark value (which failed outright), bg.warning's old dark value (amber.500) already cleared the 3:1 non-text floor at 3.05:1, but only barely — the new dark value (amber.300) clears it comfortably at 5.80:1, so every former bg.warning-indicator consumer now uses this token directly. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

warning-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.warning, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-warning on amber.700 = 6.96:1, passes AA. Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — light value unchanged. Dark value moved from amber.400 to amber.200, one step lighter, following bg.warning's own dark move to amber.300 (keeping the same relative hover-lightening gap). text.on-warning (amber.900 as of this change) on amber.200 (dark) = 10.54:1.

warning-subtle.$description: Moved from amber.100 to amber.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (amber.900 → amber.950). text.warning (amber.800 at the time) on amber.50 = 9.74:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.90:1 on amber.100). Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated light tint, independent of text.warning's own value.

warning-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses warning-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (amber.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.warning (amber.800 at the time) on amber.100 = 8.90:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching warning-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation.

success.$description: Solid fill hosting text.on-success. green.600 (pre-OKLCH-regen step) gave neither white nor gray.950 text 4.5:1 (4.39:1 / 4.13:1) — green.700 gives white text 6.50:1 (verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4).

success-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.success, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-success on green.800 = 9.56:1, passes AA.

success-subtle.$description: Moved from green.100 to green.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (green.900 → green.950). text.success (green.800) on green.50 = 9.15:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.42:1 on green.100).

success-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses success-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (green.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.success (green.800) on green.100 = 8.42:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching success-subtle's own brand-independence.

success-indicator.$description: New token (2026-08-16), found reviewing Badge's dot mode — for non-text graphical status indicators, distinct from bg.success (green.700), which is only verified as a background *for text*. green.500 vs bg.surface (white) = 3.07:1 — the tightest margin of the four indicator tokens, but still clears the 3:1 floor (the same primitive step border.success already uses for the identical reason, Phase 15). Dark theme uses green.400 instead (4.57:1) — see that theme's own description for why bg.success's own dark value only barely clears this floor. Shared across both brand themes, matching every other status-tone token's brand-independence.

info-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.info, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-info on blue.700 = 6.93:1, passes AA.

info-subtle.$description: Moved from blue.100 to blue.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (blue.900 → blue.950, the mirror-opposite extreme) to preserve the same relative gap. text.info (blue.700) on blue.50 = 6.63:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.10:1 on blue.100).

info-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses info-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (blue.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.info (blue.700) on blue.100 = 6.10:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching info-subtle's own brand-independence.

info-indicator.$description: New token (2026-08-16), found reviewing Badge's dot mode — for non-text graphical status indicators, distinct from bg.info (blue.600), which is only verified as a background *for text*. blue.500 vs bg.surface (white) = 3.26:1. Dark theme uses blue.400 instead (4.35:1) — see that theme's own description for why bg.info's own dark value only barely clears this floor. Shared across both brand themes, matching every other status-tone token's brand-independence.

neutral.$description: Fifth status-tone fill, for neutral/offline-style indicators (e.g. Avatar's offline status dot). gray.500 on bg.surface: 3.25:1 light / 3.10:1 dark, both pass WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1) — re-verified 2026-07-18 (Phase 4, OKLCH regen), shared across all 4 themes since gray.500 uniquely satisfies both. (Dark figure corrected 2026-08-16 — the previously-recorded 4.34:1 was gray.400's own contrast against this same surface, not gray.500's; the token's actual value was never wrong, only this description's cited number. Found while adding bg.danger/warning/success/info-indicator, which needed the same gray.400-vs-gray.500 distinction checked carefully.)

neutral-strong.$description: Solid neutral fill for hosting text (Badge's solid variant, neutral tone) — bg.neutral (gray.500) is only verified for the 3:1 non-text case. gray.600 with white text gives 4.70:1, passing everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

neutral-strong-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-17), found adding Tag's whole-tag clickable/selectable mode — bg.neutral-strong's own hover step. Unlike every other *-hover token, uses the SAME value (gray.700) in both light and dark themes rather than the usual darken-in-light/lighten-in-dark split: bg.neutral-strong itself is already brand-and-mode-agnostic (gray.600 in all 4 themes, see its own description above), and lightening toward gray.500 for a dark-mode hover fails AA against text.on-neutral (white on gray.500 = 3.25:1, below the 4.5:1 floor) — a documented exception, same class as bg.danger-hover/bg.brand-hover's own original dark-mode direction overrides (see 03-token-system-spec.md's Phase 3 notes). White text.on-neutral on gray.700 = 6.88:1, comfortably passes AA in both modes.

skeleton.$description: New token (2026-08-16), added for Skeleton — bg.subtle (gray.50) was the original fill, but measured directly against bg.surface (white) it is only 1.04:1, functionally invisible for a component whose entire purpose is to read as a visible placeholder shape (found reviewing Skeleton). Not a WCAG-text-contrast failure (Skeleton is decorative/aria-hidden, exempt like disabled controls) but a real functional gap — the same class of issue Phase 16's bg.*-indicator tokens closed for Badge's dot mode: an existing token verified for one purpose (bg.subtle: hover fill, dashboard panel, neutral accent) reused for a new one (a standalone visible graphic) it was never checked against. Revised same day from gray.200 to emerald.200 at explicit direction, to give the skeleton fill brand identity instead of staying neutral. emerald.200 vs bg.surface = 1.34:1 — effectively identical visual weight to gray.200's own 1.35:1 (deliberately matched, not coincidental), so the visibility fix carries over unchanged; only the hue changed. Brand-specific (unlike bg.neutral/bg.code's brand-agnostic precedent, since the whole point here is to carry brand identity) — see purple-light.json for that theme's own value.

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision.

code.$description: New token (2026-08-08) for inline code/token-reference pills in Storybook documentation (docs.css's .dbm-tokentable code) — mirrors bg.info-subtle's exact blue.50/blue.950 lightness-curve values, but under a name that doesn't imply status/info meaning, since a plain code reference isn't a status. Not currently consumed by any published component (the real Code.tsx atom uses bg.subtle instead) — Storybook-docs-only for now.

tertiary.$description: gray.500 fails AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder). gray.600 gives 4.70:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen), still lighter/more muted than text.secondary (gray.700).

on-danger.$description: Text on a solid bg.danger fill. White on red.600 = 5.10:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use red.900 instead (changed 2026-08-20 from gray.950, as part of the danger token consolidation — see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json's own description).

on-info.$description: Text on a solid bg.info fill (Badge solid variant). White on blue.600 = 4.71:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use gray.950 instead — see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json.

on-success.$description: Text on a solid bg.success fill (Badge solid variant). Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): light-theme bg.success is green.700, where white gives 6.50:1. Dark theme keeps gray.950 against green.500 (5.91:1) — white fails there (3.07:1) — so this token is now theme-specific rather than shared; see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json.

on-warning.$description: Text on a solid bg.warning fill. White on amber.600 = 4.78:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use amber.900 instead (changed 2026-08-20 from gray.950, as part of the warning token consolidation — see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json's own description).

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral-strong fill (Badge solid variant). White on gray.600 = 4.70:1, passes everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

link.$description: emerald.600 (the brand anchor) on bg.surface is 4.16:1, failing AA as literal text (a pre-existing gap, unrelated to the Phase 4 regen — it just hadn't been checked before). emerald.700 gives 6.08:1 (verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4).

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links (see text.link). Reuses the same resolved value as text.link: emerald.600 (the literal brand anchor) on white is only 4.16:1, failing AA — emerald.700 gives 6.08:1.

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.700 to red.600, so text.danger now shares the same primitive step as bg.danger/border.danger/icon.danger in light mode. red.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 5.10:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 7.39:1). See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full rationale and contrast table.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.800 to amber.600, so text.warning now shares the same primitive step as bg.warning/border.warning/icon.warning in light mode. amber.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.78:1, still passes AA (was 10.14:1) — a bigger margin drop than danger's own equivalent move, since amber.800 sat unusually high on the scale to begin with; still a real, deliberate pass, not a near-miss. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full rationale and contrast table.

success.$description: green.800 on bg.success-subtle (green.100) gives 8.42:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen — originally fixed in Phase 3 when the HSL-derived scales gave green.700 only 4.08:1, failing AA).

neutral.$description: New token (2026-08-20) — completes the border.danger/warning/success/info/brand state-identifying family for the one tone that didn't have one yet: neutral. border.strong (gray.400), the only existing generic gray border, was measured rather than assumed and fails outright as a real border — 2.32:1 against bg.surface, well under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor (it's documented as decorative hover-state emphasis, never verified for this use). gray.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.70:1, a comfortable margin, not just a bare pass. Not currently consumed — Tag's outline variant ended up using border.neutral-strong (a richer step, added alongside this one) for its own default border instead, since a plain outline's rim needed to read as more deliberate than this token's own step; this one still completes the family for future default-emphasis use.

neutral-strong.$description: New token (2026-08-19), found adding Tag's selectable solid-variant ring — needed a neutral border richer than border.strong (gray.400) to read clearly as an offset-halo accent against bg.surface. Reuses the same primitive step text.secondary already uses (gray.700), but as its own independently-tracked border token rather than reusing text.secondary directly — border.* and text.* are separate categories specifically so they can diverge later without side effects on each other. gray.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.88:1.

focus.$description: emerald.500 on bg.surface fell just short of the 3:1 non-text floor (2.92:1) after the Phase 4 OKLCH regen. emerald.600 gives 4.16:1 (verified 2026-07-18).

brand.$description: New token (2026-08-20) — emerald counterpart to border.brand (purple); see that token's own description for its purpose. Reuses bg.brand's own light-mode step (emerald.700, not the numerically-parallel emerald.600 — emerald needs to go one step further than purple's own analogous step to reach equivalent perceptual/contrast weight, the same reason border.focus's own emerald value sits at .600 while purple's sits at .500). emerald.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.08:1, clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor comfortably.

brand-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.brand (2026-08-20), for naming consistency with its sibling family tokens (border.danger-subtle/warning-subtle/success-subtle/info-subtle all carry the -subtle suffix for the same decorative-only role; this one hadn't, despite being the exact same kind of token). Value unchanged. Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from emerald.600). emerald.100 on white is only 1.13:1, well below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor — deliberately accepted, since this token is for decorative UI accents rather than a border that identifies a component/state boundary (border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying). No longer literal across every theme as of 2026-08-16 — dark mode moved to emerald.900 (see that file's own description) so each mode gets its own similarly-subtle contrast ratio instead of sharing one literal value that read very differently against each mode's background.

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.500 to red.600, so border.danger now shares the same primitive step as bg.danger/text.danger/icon.danger in light mode, and absorbs border.danger-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer, e.g. Tag's outline-danger border and solid-danger selected-ring accent, now uses this token directly). red.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 5.10:1, an improvement over the previous 3.48:1. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

danger-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same family.100-light/family.900-dark scale step as border.brand-subtle — not a reuse of border.danger (red.600, the stronger state-identifying border used for e.g. Input validation, where WCAG 1.4.11 actually applies). Pairs with bg.danger-subtle (red.50) for any component drawing a subtle danger-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component — first used by Avatar's `colorful` danger variant (2026-08-16), but not scoped to it. red.100 on red.50 is 1.10:1, intentionally as subtle as border.brand-subtle's 1.09:1 purple pairing. Brand-agnostic — identical value in every brand theme, same as bg.danger-subtle. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.500 to amber.600, so border.warning now shares the same primitive step as bg.warning/text.warning/icon.warning in light mode, and absorbs border.warning-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer, e.g. Tag's outline-warning border and solid-warning selected-ring accent, now uses this token directly). amber.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.78:1, an improvement over the previous 3.31:1. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

warning-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.warning-subtle (amber.50) for any component's warning-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. amber.100 on amber.50 is 1.09:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

success.$description: Added 2026-08-16 to complete the state-family set alongside border.danger — same amber.500-equivalent scale step (green.500) for a success-toned state-identifying border.

success-strong.$description: New token (2026-08-19), same rationale danger's and warning's own now-retired -strong tokens originally established (Phase 20; both were folded into their base border.* token in the 2026-08-20 consolidations, but success/info/neutral keep their own separate -strong tier for now). Reuses text.success's own primitive step (green.800), independently tracked. green.800 vs bg.surface (white) = 9.56:1.

success-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.success-subtle (green.50) for any component's success-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. green.100 on green.50 is 1.09:1. Brand-agnostic.

info.$description: Added 2026-08-16 to complete the state-family set alongside border.danger — same scale step (blue.500) for an info-toned state-identifying border.

info-strong.$description: New token (2026-08-19), same rationale danger's and warning's own now-retired -strong tokens originally established (Phase 20; both were folded into their base border.* token in the 2026-08-20 consolidations, but success/info/neutral keep their own separate -strong tier for now). Reuses text.info's own primitive step (blue.700), independently tracked. blue.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.93:1.

info-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.info-subtle (blue.50) for any component's info-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. blue.100 on blue.50 is 1.09:1. Brand-agnostic.

code.$description: Paired with bg.code (2026-08-08) — blue.100/blue.900, a purely decorative border, not one that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply — same accepted class as border.brand-subtle. Measures 1.09:1 light / 1.28:1 dark against bg.code, an accepted tradeoff, not an oversight.

secondary.$description: gray.400 on bg.surface was 2.32:1, failing the WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor (3:1) — found during the Phase 4 icon-contrast sweep (2026-07-18) while this token was still unused by any shipped component. gray.500 gives 3.25:1, and stays more muted than icon.default (gray.600, 4.70:1).

danger.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the danger token consolidation — shares the same primitive step as bg.danger/text.danger/border.danger (red.600 light / red.300 dark) rather than a distinct icon-specific value. Standalone danger-tone icon, not one sitting on a solid bg.danger fill (see icon.on-danger for that case). red.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 5.10:1.

on-danger.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the danger token consolidation — same value as text.on-danger (white light / red.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.danger fill (e.g. inside a danger Button/IconButton). White on red.600 = 5.10:1.

warning.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the warning token consolidation — shares the same primitive step as bg.warning/text.warning/border.warning (amber.600 light / amber.300 dark) rather than a distinct icon-specific value. Standalone warning-tone icon, not one sitting on a solid bg.warning fill (see icon.on-warning for that case). amber.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.78:1.

on-warning.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the warning token consolidation — same value as text.on-warning (white light / amber.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.warning fill. White on amber.600 = 4.78:1.
